findings.issue: The kana transcription contains きごう ('symbol') three times where the jp has spaces — a tokenizer artifact (space tokens were assigned reading きごう). A learner reading the kana would read nonsense syllables.
findings.current: このきごうりょうりのきごうつくりかたわきごうかんたんです
findings.suggested: このりょうりのつくりかたわかんたんです

findings.issue: Same artifact as kana: 'kigou' inserted three times where the jp has spaces. This is not the known punctuation/katakana issue — it adds nonexistent syllables to the sentence's phonetics.
Space-separator tokens were given the reading きごう ('symbol'). Same defect on tokens[4].r and tokens[8].r. This is the root cause of the corrupted kana/romaji; a space has no reading.
findings.suggested: null (space has no reading; or drop the space tokens)

findings.issue: 料理 means 'cooking/the act of cooking', not the room 'kitchen' (台所). The natural translation shifts the topic from the activity to a location, contradicting lit_en ('As for cooking') and expl_en itself.
findings.current: In the kitchen, first we cut the vegetables.
findings.suggested: When cooking, first you cut the vegetables.

findings.issue: 'Na cozinha' reads as the physical room (台所), but 料理は is the activity of cooking. Contradicts lit_pt ('Quanto a cozinhar') and expl_pt.
findings.current: Na cozinha, primeiro a gente corta os legumes.
findings.suggested: Ao cozinhar, primeiro a gente corta os legumes.

findings.issue: The literal mirror topicalizes the interrogative phrase ('Quanto a qual trem'), but どの電車に is the に-complement of 乗る, not a topic (interrogatives cannot be topics). Also broken Portuguese. lit_en correctly renders it without topicalization.

Tokens 0 (小/しょう) and 1 (学校/がっこう) are glossless fragments duplicating token 2, the combined 小学校. The token sequence no longer tiles the sentence (reconstruction yields 小学校小学校の前で…), unlike every other item in the batch.
findings.current: 小 + 学校 fragment tokens preceding the combined 小学校 token
findings.suggested: Remove the two fragment tokens; keep only the combined 小学校 token.

findings.issue: Tokens 0 (長/なが) and 1 (さ/さ) are glossless fragments prepended before 彼, duplicating the combined 長さ token that appears later in its correct position. The token sequence does not tile the sentence.
findings.current: 長 + さ fragment tokens prepended before 彼
findings.suggested: Remove the two fragment tokens; keep only the in-place 長さ token.

findings.issue: The literal mirror presents 長さに as a topic ('As for...'), but に marks the cause of 疲れた — as expl_en itself states ('points to the cause/target of the tiredness'). The mirror misrepresents the particle structure.
findings.current: As for the length of his talk, I got tired.
findings.suggested: By the length of his talk, (I) got tired.

findings.issue: Same as lit_en: 'Quanto à' presents the に-marked cause as a topic, contradicting expl_pt ('aponta a causa/alvo do cansaço'). The Quanto-a device belongs to は topics, not に complements.
findings.current: Quanto à extensão da conversa dele, (eu) me cansei.
findings.suggested: Com a extensão da conversa dele, (eu) me cansei.

findings.issue: The literal mirror uses the topic device ('As for the bird, it...') for 鳥が, but が marks the subject, not a topic — expl_en itself says 鳥が is the subject, and the corpus elsewhere mirrors が as '(subject)' (cf. この大きい荷物が邪魔だ). Blurs the taught は/が distinction.
findings.current: As for the bird, it, toward the south, goes flying.
findings.suggested: The bird (subject), toward the south, goes flying.

findings.issue: Same as lit_en: 'Quanto ao pássaro, ele...' mirrors the が-marked subject with the は-topic device plus a resumptive pronoun, contradicting expl_pt (sujeito) and the corpus convention for が.
findings.current: Quanto ao pássaro, ele, em direção ao sul, vai voando.
findings.suggested: O pássaro (sujeito), em direção ao sul, vai voando.
